parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
A wire of cross-sectional area A is made from metal of resistivity ρ. The wire is extended.
Assume that the volume V of the wire remains constant as it extends.
Show that the resistance R of the extending wire is inversely proportional to A^{2}.
parts.question_text_latex:
A wire of cross-sectional area A is made from metal of resistivity $\rho$. The wire is extended.
Assume that the volume V of the wire remains constant as it extends.
Show that the resistance R of the extending wire is inversely proportional to $A^{2}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
A battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) E and internal resistance r is connected to a variable
resistor of resistance R, as shown in Fig. 6.1.
The current in the circuit is I.
Use Kirchhoff’s second law to show that
^{R}^{=}((E)/(I))^{-}^{r}^{.}
parts.question_text_latex:
A battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) E and internal resistance r is connected to a variable
resistor of resistance R, as shown in Fig. 6.1.
The current in the circuit is I.
Use Kirchhoff’s second law to show that
$^{\mathrm{R}}^{=}(\frac{E}{I})^{-}^{\mathrm{r}}^{.}$
